chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs34768248
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at chr5:1295601 in glioblastoma-relevant cells.
The G>A change alone does not alter TERT expression or a disease-relevant phenotype.
Any TERT association is driven by a linked causal variant rather than this base.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP or footprinting in glioblastoma cells shows reproducible ref-G enrichment at chr5:1295601.
An allele-specific reporter/MPRA in a TERT-expressing glioblastoma line shows a G>A effect at this base after controlling for linked variants.
CTCF perturbation at this element changes TERT expression in cis in a glioblastoma-relevant cell type.

chains.title: CTCF binding at a TERT upstream element
chains.element: TERT upstream ENSR5_C5GP enhancer/promoter-proximal region; variant is not inside an annotated ENCODE cCRE and lies 75 bp from a pELS
chains.cell_type: glioblastoma/glial-lineage cells; CTCF occupancy has been seen only in H9 neural progenitor cells

links.claim: CTCF is the candidate TF, with ref G hypothesized to bind more strongly than alt A. CTCF has no QBiC-SELEX model in the provided evidence, so the direction is not measured. CTCF ChIP peaks containing the variant are reported only in H9/neural progenitor cells, not in the glioblastoma expression context; E19 explicitly reports no glioblastoma CTCF peak.

The variant lies in the computationally annotated TERT upstream ENSR5_C5GP enhancer. It is not contained in an ENCODE cCRE; the nearest pELS is 75 bp away, so the active-element evidence does not overlap the base.

TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.5 kb upstream, and is the best L2G gene in the available credible set. Caveat: that credible set is for hypertension with PIP 0.00, not glioblastoma/melanoma/bladder cancer.
CTCF is expressed in glioblastoma lines, but glioblastoma CTCF occupancy at this base is not established. The only reported CTCF peaks containing the variant are in H9 neural progenitor cells.

TERT is broadly implicated in glioblastoma, melanoma and bladder cancer, but this variant has no direct GWAS Catalog association and no significant GTEx eQTL. Phenotype support is therefore gene-level and not variant-specific.

predictions: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP-qPCR in glioblastoma or neural progenitor cells will show preferential ref-G binding at chr5:1295601.
The ref-G allele preserves a CTCF-binding motif that alt A weakens.
CTCF perturbation at this element changes TERT expression in the relevant neural-lineage context.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP-qPCR or footprinting in glioblastoma cells shows no occupancy or no ref-G enrichment at this base.
The G>A change does not alter CTCF binding in vitro or in a neural-lineage cell context.
CTCF perturbation at this element does not change TERT expression in the relevant cell type.

matrix.test: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP-qPCR at rs34768248 in a glioblastoma cell line

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-specific CTCF occupancy at chr5:1295601 in glioblastoma cells.
Ref-G enrichment in CTCF ChIP-qPCR or allele-specific footprinting in glioblastoma/neural-lineage cells.
No CTCF allele-specific effect; any signal would not support the JUN-gain model.

matrix.test: Allele-specific luciferase reporter or MPRA for G vs A in a TERT-expressing glioblastoma line

outcomes.outcome: No allele-specific reporter/MPRA effect for G>A.
Ref-G-dependent change consistent with CTCF binding, but activity direction could be activation or repression.
Alt-A-dependent change consistent with AP-1/JUN gain.

matrix.test: Allele-specific JUN ChIP-qPCR at rs34768248 in a glioblastoma cell line

outcomes.outcome: No alt-A-specific JUN occupancy at this base.
No JUN allele-specific effect; CTCF model unaffected.
Alt-A enrichment in JUN ChIP-qPCR in glioblastoma cells.

matrix.test: CRISPRi/dCas9 perturbation of the TERT upstream element plus TERT qPCR in glioblastoma cells

outcomes.outcome: No change in TERT expression after local CRISPRi/dCas9 perturbation of the element.
CTCF-dependent change in TERT expression, preferentially in the ref-G context.
JUN-dependent change in TERT expression, preferentially in the alt-A context.

next_experiment: The single cheapest experiment that separates the top two chains (H0 vs H1) is allele-specific CTCF ChIP-qPCR at rs34768248 in a glioblastoma cell line. H0 predicts no reproducible allele-specific CTCF occupancy; H1 predicts ref-G enrichment. If glioblastoma CTCF occupancy is absent, repeat in H9 neural progenitor cells as a lower-disease-relevance fallback to test the H1 binding link, but that fallback alone would not establish glioblastoma relevance.
